nodes.description: Oral lipid-conjugated cidofovir prodrug approved for smallpox under the FDA Animal Rule; it acts as a nucleotide analogue DNA polymerase inhibitor with surrogate efficacy in mousepox and rabbitpox models.

evidence.snippet: Brincidofovir adds a second oral agent to treat smallpox, with a different mechanism of action than tecovirimat.

evidence.snippet: Two surrogate animal models were included in the Food and Drug Administration's (FDA) decision to approve brincidofovir: ectromelia virus in mice and rabbitpox in rabbits.

evidence.snippet: Pockmarks were caused by the destruction of sebaceous glands and formation of granulation tissue; they occurred all over the body but were most prominent on the face because of the large number of sebaceous glands located there.

nodes.description: Inhaled variola seeded the oropharyngeal or respiratory mucosa, infected macrophages, drained along local lymphatics, and replicated in regional lymph nodes, spleen, bone marrow, and distant lymph nodes before symptoms.

evidence.snippet: Macrophages were among the early sites/cells of infection, and the virus migrated along the local lymphatic channels and multiplied in regional lymph nodes.

nodes.description: Vaccinia-based vaccination prevents smallpox and was used with case isolation and contact tracing in ring-vaccination strategies; a prompt post-exposure dose can attenuate or prevent disease.

evidence.reference_title: Countermeasures and vaccination against terrorism using smallpox: pre-event and post-event smallpox vaccination and its contraindications.
evidence.snippet: Core components of the public health management of a terrorism attack using smallpox are: vaccination (ring vaccination and mass vaccination), adverse event monitoring, confirmed and suspected smallpox case management, contact management, identifying, tracing, monitoring contacts, and quarantine.

nodes.description: Oral orthopoxvirus antiviral approved for smallpox under the FDA Animal Rule; it inhibits the conserved p37/VP37 envelope protein and prevents formation and egress of enveloped virions.

evidence.reference_title: Oral Tecovirimat for the Treatment of Smallpox.
evidence.snippet: Tecovirimat inhibits p37, a protein that is present and highly conserved (approximately 98% amino acid identity) in all orthopoxviruses; the inhibition of p37 prevents the formation and egress of enveloped virions, which are essential for virulence.

evidence.reference_title: Oral Tecovirimat for the Treatment of Smallpox.
evidence.snippet: In pilot studies, tecovirimat was shown to provide protective efficacy in multiple small-animal and nonhuman primate models of orthopoxvirus disease.

nodes.description: Variola encodes numerous terminal-region immunomodulatory proteins, including SPICE and a high-affinity CC-chemokine-binding protein, that blunt complement and chemokine-mediated antiviral immunity.

evidence.reference_title: Variola virus immune evasion proteins.
evidence.snippet: Both SPICE and VCP are similar in structure and function to the family of mammalian complement regulatory proteins, which function to prevent inadvertent injury to adjacent cells and tissues during complement activation.

evidence.reference_title: Variola virus immune evasion proteins.
evidence.snippet: The second variola protein is the variola virus high-affinity secreted chemokine-binding protein type II (CKBP-II, CBP-II, vCCI), which binds CC-chemokine receptors.
